resources.string: Archived observation, not a live telescope view. Image colours may represent wavelengths invisible to the eye.
Brightest star in the night sky. Physical values refer to Sirius A; Sirius B is its white-dwarf companion. Catalogue position and approximate distance.
Variable red supergiant in Orion. Radius, distance and present-day mass range are model dependent; brightness changes over time.

Saturn’s largest moon, with a dense nitrogen atmosphere and methane lakes. Huygens temperature and pressure are reference measurements from its 2005 landing site. Cassini near-infrared surface mosaic; NASA/JPL trajectories.
Star-forming nebula in Orion. Pointing and daily path follow its catalogue centre. A nebula has no single planetary surface.
Open star cluster in Taurus. Pointing follows the cluster centre. The WISE infrared image shows stars and surrounding dust.

Andromeda (M31) is a spiral galaxy about 2.5 million light-years away. M31* is its central black hole: the tabulated black-hole mass belongs to M31*, not the entire galaxy. The photograph shows the galaxy.
